# Vendored Highlightr

Forked from [raspu/Highlightr](https://github.com/raspu/Highlightr) at **2.3.0**
(`05e7fcc63b33925cd0c1faaa205cdd5681e7bbef`), with one change.

## Why

`Highlightr.init` reads its themes and `highlight.min.js` from
`Bundle.module`. SwiftPM generates that accessor from the dependency's
`swift-tools-version:5.3`, and it checks exactly two paths:

```swift
let mainPath  = Bundle.main.bundleURL.appendingPathComponent("Highlightr_Highlightr.bundle").path
let buildPath = "/Users/<whoever-built-it>/.../.build/release/Highlightr_Highlightr.bundle"
```

`bundleURL` is the `.app` directory itself, not `Contents/Resources` — and
macOS refuses to sign a bundle with anything loose at its root, so the
resource bundle cannot legally go there. That leaves only `buildPath`, an
absolute path into the build machine's checkout.

The result: the app runs on the machine that compiled it and dies at launch
on every other one, with a `fatalError` inside `Bundle.module`. It is not
caught by a build or by tests, because both run where `buildPath` exists.

## The change

`src/classes/Highlightr.swift` looks in `Contents/Resources` first and falls
back to `Bundle.module`, so `swift run` and tests behave exactly as before.

Upstream cannot fix this in the library — the accessor is generated by
SwiftPM, not written by Highlightr.

## Updating

Re-copy the upstream source and reapply that one edit; it is marked
`DIFFT PATCH` in the file.
